    Jhon Caldas v. City of Union (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-02191 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-02191-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the District Court's dismissal of Jhon Caldas's civil rights complaint alleging that acoustic devices damaged his hearing and organs in Fall 2024 and that his water, air, and electronics were interfered with. Caldas appealed the dismissals of his complaint and motions for preliminary injunction and counsel appointment but forfeited most of his arguments by failing to develop them in his opening brief. The court agreed with the District Court that the complaint did not state a viable claim. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    United States v. Barton (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca10-25-06176 / USCOURTS-ca10-25-06176-0

    FAPD-AI: Ronnie Allen Barton's appeal of his conviction for attempted coercion and enticement of minors, sex offense by a registered sex offender, and attempted receipt of child pornography was dismissed as wholly frivolous. The Tenth Circuit affirmed that evidence sufficiently established every element of his convictions and that his sentence of 25 years imprisonment (180 months concurrent on certain counts, 120 months consecutive on another, plus lifetime supervised release) was properly imposed. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Modernization of Regulations Under 9 CFR Parts 101-118 and 123-124 (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE · FR-2026-09-11 / 2026-18531

    official summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) proffers this Request for Information (RFI) to solicit the public's input on regulatory considerations related to 9 CFR parts 101-118, 123-124. The regulations are issued primarily pursuant to Section 154 of the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act (VSTA). USDA intends to evaluate each part and subpart for its effectiveness at upholding the VSTA's statutory mandate to prohibit the preparation, sale, barter, or exchange of “worthless, contaminated, dangerous, or harmful” viruses, serums, toxins, or analogous products intended for the use in the treatment of domestic animals, i.e., all animals, other than man, including poultry. The current regulations reflect decades of incremental amendments, technical updates, and revisions adopted at different points in time to address specific scientific, operational, and/or programmatic needs; in recent history, USDA has not holistically reformed the regulations implementing the VSTA. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-02

    Protecting Against National Security Threats to the Communications Supply Chain Through the Equipment Authorization Pro… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FEDERAL COMMUNICATIONS COMMISSION · FR-2026-09-11 / 2026-18535

    official summary: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) takes further steps to strengthen its equipment authorization program against national security risks to the communications supply chain. The Commission closes a component-part loophole by prohibiting authorization of devices that incorporate logic-bearing hardware components produced by an entity identified on the Commission's Covered List, where the device would itself be prohibited from authorization had the Covered List entity produced the entire device. The Commission also requires that any modification or permissive change to equipment by an entity identified on the Covered List undergo full certification, clarifies that its marketing rules reach any entity (including online marketplaces) that markets unauthorized equipment, and requires online marketplaces, subject to limited exceptions, to display a device's FCC ID at the online point of sale. Finally, the Commission amends its definition of “critical infrastructure,” as used on the Covered List, and corrects two administrative errors in its rules. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: This final rule makes the following changes to the National Network (NN) in Syracuse, New York: the de-designation of the segment of the NN from Interstate 81 (I-81) between the New York, Susquehanna, and Western Railway bridge and the I-81/I-690 interchange (I-81 Viaduct); and the addition to the NN of the signalized surface urban arterial roadway system (Community Grid) that replaces the I-81 Viaduct and is designated as part of Business Loop 81 (BL 81). The remainder of I-81 between the I-81/I-690 interchange and the I-81/I-481 interchange (Exit 29) will be reclassified as BL 81 and remain on the NN. Interstate 481 (I-481) will be reclassified as I-81 and will remain on the NN. This rule will become effective immediately. FR-SEL-01

    Adjusting Certain Delegations Under the Defense Production Act (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-09-11 / 2026-18739

    FAPD-AI: Executive Order 14427 amends the delegations of Defense Production Act authority, adding the Secretary of the Interior alongside the Secretary of Energy for energy-related matters, with each able to exercise authority independently. The order establishes a dispute resolution process for disagreements between the two Secretaries, routing disputes to the National Energy Dominance Council and, if military operations or national defense infrastructure are involved, also to the National Security Council. The order extends certain Defense Production Act authorities to the Secretary of the Interior and Secretary of Commerce. FR-SEL-03

    118 HR 2317 RH: Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr2317rh

    FAPD-AI: The Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2026 authorizes the transfer of approximately 67 acres of Forest Service land to Nevada for state parks and conservation, and conveys approximately 7,777 acres to Douglas County for flood control and recreation purposes. The bill authorizes the sale of federal lands across northern Nevada, establishes wilderness areas, transfers land to the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California held in trust, and provides for land conveyances to various Nevada cities and counties for fire protection, flood management, and economic development. The act includes provisions for public-purposes conveyances by the Forest Service and specifies restrictions on use and reversion conditions. BILLS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 00:29:28 Eastern time ET
    119 HR 4931 RH: National Park System Long-Term Lease Investment Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr4931rh

    FAPD-AI: The National Park System Long-Term Lease Investment Act authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to extend certain existing leases within National Park System units without opening them to competitive bidding if the lessee has held the lease for at least five years, is in compliance with lease terms, and the extension is consistent with park unit purposes. The act limits such extensions to one per lease without re-bidding and requires the Secretary to revise relevant regulations within 90 days of enactment. BILLS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 00:29:28 Eastern time ET
    119 HR 9327 RH: Providing Emotional Assistance with Relief and Love Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9327rh

    FAPD-AI: The Providing Emotional Assistance with Relief and Love Act (PEARL Act) establishes a pilot program within U.S. Customs and Border Protection to adopt dogs from local animal shelters and train them as support dogs for CBP's Support Canine Program. The Secretary of Homeland Security must establish the pilot program within 60 days of enactment, with a three-year duration. BILLS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 00:29:28 Eastern time ET
    119 HR 9340 RH: Ratepayer Protection Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9340rh

    FAPD-AI: The Ratepayer Protection Act amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to establish a federal standard requiring electric utilities to recover the full incremental costs of generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades from large-load customers—defined as non-residential consumers with peak electric demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site for data storage and computational applications. The act requires large-load customers to provide financial assurances or contributions to cover upgrade costs and mandates that state regulatory authorities and nonregulated utilities consider and make determinations on this standard within one to two years of enactment. BILLS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 00:29:28 Eastern time ET
    91 HR 9342 RH: GPO Modernization Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9342rh

    FAPD-AI: The GPO Modernization Act of 2026 revises the authorities of the Government Publishing Office to modernize sales programs for government documents, establish public information programs under the Superintendent of Documents, and ensure equitable public access to government publications through the Federal Depository Library Program. The act updates GPO operational authorities, modernizes Congressional publishing procedures, clarifies the relationship between GPO and the Federal Register, and repeals the requirement for the Congressional Research Service to prepare a hardbound version of the Annotated Constitution. BILLS-SEL-01

    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9360rh

    FAPD-AI: The Advisory Committee on the Records of Congress Sunset Act sunsets the Advisory Committee on the Records of Congress effective 60 days after enactment and transfers its responsibilities to the Director of the Center for Legislative Archives. The act establishes requirements for annual reporting on Congressional records management and preservation to relevant congressional committees, and mandates that the Archivist of the United States, Secretary of the Senate, and Clerk of the House meet periodically to review records management practices. BILLS-SEL-01

    107 HR 9394 RH: Civil Preparedness for Agroterrorism Exercise Act of 2026 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9394rh

    FAPD-AI: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to conduct an exercise within four years to test preparedness for agroterrorism against U.S. agricultural and food infrastructure sectors. The exercise must include scenarios involving transportation and deployment of biological agents and require coordination with federal, state, local, tribal, territorial, and private sector entities. The Secretary must submit an after-action report to Congress within 180 days of exercise completion containing findings, lessons learned, and recommended legislative actions for improving security posture. BILLS-SEL-01
